notes: TBox rule edit, added for the 0020 slot (fluid mechanics, for variety). Derivability very_unlikely: rising viscosity with shear rate is the definition of a dilatant (shear-thickening) fluid, stated in general form in Wikipedia's first sentence and copied widely; it follows from nothing more basic. No exceptions: a fluid whose viscosity falls with shear rate is shear-thinning (pseudoplastic) by definition. Counterfactual: clearly false, and the commonest confusion in the topic (shear-thinning ketchup). The class name 'dilatant' (from dilatancy, volume increase) and its zh/es forms (胀流型, dilatante) do not state the answer; 'shear thickening' would, so it is never used in a prompt. Determinate queries use invented fluids named in the prompt (Brennite gel, DX-14). The indeterminate queries use oobleck, whose behaviour is stated by name very often ('oobleck' AND 'acts like a solid' 185) while its class is stated less often (it is usually called non-Newtonian), so both turn on the same storage choice: two worlds. w2 is the less likely world but valid: lopsided worlds are kept (Decisions 4). Step 3: in w1 oobleck leaves the class of dilatant fluids (a classification), keeping its behaviour; it stays non-Newtonian (viscosity still changes with shear), so nothing outside the chain is contradicted. In w2 oobleck thins when struck; this contradicts only facts about oobleck itself (side facts of the stored behaviour giving way, such as people running across cornstarch pools), as the Sun burning helium does in 0005. R1 nuance: dense cornstarch suspensions thin slightly at very low shear rates before thickening; the oobleck prompts ask about striking or stirring quickly, where thickening is clear. Oobleck prompts never assert that it is dilatant. Near query (SI unit of dynamic viscosity, pascal-second) shares the topic, does not depend on the rule and differs from the new answer. Relation viscosity_under_shear is new and property-free (relations/physics.tbox3.md). Verifier (tbox3 review): the class's other name 'shear-thickening fluid' is a restatement of the edited rule and gives way with it (it is never used in a prompt).
